title: Esther Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Esther chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Esther Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Esther Chapter 6.

questions.question: What did the king command to be brought to him when he could not sleep?
options: The book of records of the chronicles
questions.correctAnswer: The book of records of the chronicles
questions.explanation: The king commanded to bring the book of records of the chronicles because he could not sleep, as stated in Esther 6:1.

questions.question: Who sought to lay hands on King Ahasuerus?
questions.explanation: Bigthana and Teresh were the two chamberlains who sought to lay hands on King Ahasuerus, as mentioned in Esther 6:2.

questions.question: What did the king ask regarding Mordecai's actions?
options: What reward has been given to him?
questions.correctAnswer: What reward has been given to him?
questions.explanation: The king asked, 'What honour and dignity hath been done to Mordecai for this?' as indicated in Esther 6:3.

questions.question: Who was in the outward court when the king asked who was there?
questions.explanation: Haman was in the outward court, as stated in Esther 6:4.

questions.question: What did the king's servants say when asked about Haman?
options: He is waiting for an audience
questions.explanation: The king's servants informed him that Haman standeth in the court, as mentioned in Esther 6:5.

questions.question: True or False: The king could not sleep on the night referred to in Esther 6.
questions.explanation: The chapter begins with the statement that the king could not sleep, indicating it is true, as stated in Esther 6:1.

questions.question: True or False: Mordecai was rewarded for his actions before this night.
questions.explanation: The king's servants stated that nothing had been done for Mordecai, indicating he was not rewarded before this night, as noted in Esther 6:3.

questions.question: True or False: The king ordered Haman to be executed immediately.
questions.explanation: The king asked Haman what should be done to honor a man, and did not order Haman's execution at this point, as seen in Esther 6:6.

questions.question: True or False: Mordecai was honored by being paraded through the city.
questions.explanation: Mordecai was honored by being arrayed and paraded through the city on horseback, as described in Esther 6:11.

questions.question: What did Haman think when asked how to honor a man?
options: That it would be a public execution
That it was surely about him
That he would ignore the king's request
questions.correctAnswer: That it was surely about him
questions.explanation: Haman thought in his heart that the king would delight to honor him, as indicated in Esther 6:6.

questions.question: What was Haman's suggestion for honoring the man?
questions.explanation: Haman suggested that the man be brought the royal apparel and horse, as noted in Esther 6:8.

questions.question: What did Haman do after honoring Mordecai?
questions.explanation: After honoring Mordecai, he returned to the king's gate, as mentioned in Esther 6:12.

questions.question: What did Haman's wife and friends suggest about Mordecai?
options: He is favored by the king
questions.explanation: They warned Haman that if Mordecai is of the seed of the Jews, he would not prevail against him, as stated in Esther 6:13.

questions.question: In what order did the events in Esther 6 occur?
options: Haman entered the court, the king could not sleep
The king could not sleep, Haman entered the court
The king asked about Mordecai, Haman left
questions.correctAnswer: The king could not sleep, Haman entered the court
questions.explanation: The sequence begins with the king unable to sleep followed by Haman entering the court to ask about Mordecai, as described in Esther 6:1-4.

medium.title: Esther Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Esther Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the king ask Haman about the man whom he delights to honour?
options: What shall be done to him?
questions.correctAnswer: What shall be done to him?
questions.explanation: The king asked Haman, 'What shall be done unto the man whom the king delighteth to honour?' This shows the king's interest in honouring someone significant. (Esther 6:6)

questions.question: What did Haman suggest should be done for the man whom the king delights to honour?
questions.explanation: Haman suggested that the royal apparel be brought, along with a horse and crown, indicating a grand display of honour. (Esther 6:8)

questions.question: True or False: Haman initially believed the king was referring to him when asking about the man to honour.
questions.explanation: Haman thought to himself, 'To whom would the king delight to do honour more than to myself?' indicating he believed the king was speaking about him. (Esther 6:6)

questions.question: What did the king instruct Haman to do for Mordecai?
questions.explanation: The king instructed Haman to take the apparel and the horse and do so to Mordecai the Jew, thus honouring him as the king desired. (Esther 6:10)

questions.question: What was Haman's reaction after honouring Mordecai?
questions.explanation: Haman hasted to his house mourning after he had to honour Mordecai, showcasing his humiliation. (Esther 6:12)

questions.question: True or False: The king could not sleep because he was worried about Haman.
questions.explanation: The king could not sleep because he wanted to read the records and found out about Mordecai's loyalty, not due to worry about Haman. (Esther 6:1-2)

questions.question: What did the king's servants report to him about Mordecai?
options: Nothing had been done for him
questions.correctAnswer: Nothing had been done for him
questions.explanation: The king's servants informed him that nothing had been done for Mordecai, despite his past loyalty. (Esther 6:3)

questions.question: In what manner did Haman have to present Mordecai to the people?
questions.explanation: Haman had to array Mordecai on horseback through the city, which was part of the honour the king commanded. (Esther 6:11)

questions.question: What did the wise men and Zeresh advise Haman regarding Mordecai?
questions.explanation: They warned Haman that if Mordecai was of the Jews, he would not prevail against him but would surely fall before him. (Esther 6:13)

questions.question: What was the significance of the royal apparel and horse?
options: They were a sign of mourning
They were gifts for the king
questions.explanation: The royal apparel and horse symbolized the king's authority and the honour due to the man whom the king delighted to honour. (Esther 6:8)

questions.question: True or False: Haman was happy to carry out the king's order for Mordecai.
questions.explanation: Haman was not happy about honouring Mordecai; he was humiliated as he had intended to hang him. (Esther 6:10-12)

questions.question: What lesson does Mordecai's experience in Esther 6 teach about humility?
questions.explanation: Mordecai, who showed humility by sitting at the king's gate, was ultimately honoured by the king, demonstrating that true honour comes from God. (Esther 6:10-11)

questions.question: What does Esther 6:9 promise will happen if the king's noble prince honours someone?
questions.explanation: The verse outlines the process of public honour, indicating that the man whom the king delights to honour will be celebrated in the streets. (Esther 6:9)

hard.title: Esther Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Esther Chapter 6.

questions.question: What did Haman do after he arrayed Mordecai in royal apparel?
options: He went to the king's banquet
He hasted to his house mourning
questions.correctAnswer: He hasted to his house mourning
questions.explanation: Haman hasted to his house mourning after he arrayed Mordecai, demonstrating his dismay at the turn of events. (Esther 6:12)

questions.question: What was the fate of Haman as predicted by his wife and wise men?
options: He would be honored by the king
He would surely fall before Mordecai
He would become a servant to Mordecai
questions.correctAnswer: He would surely fall before Mordecai
questions.explanation: Haman’s wife and wise men foretold that if Mordecai was of the Jews, he would not prevail against him but would surely fall. (Esther 6:13)

questions.question: What did the king's chamberlains come to do while Haman was talking with his friends?
options: To bring Haman to the banquet
To inform him of Mordecai's honor
questions.correctAnswer: To bring Haman to the banquet
questions.explanation: The king's chamberlains came to bring Haman to the banquet that Esther had prepared. (Esther 6:14)

questions.question: What was the king's command regarding Mordecai's honor?
options: He should be paraded in royal apparel
He should be rewarded with land
He should be invited to a private audience
questions.correctAnswer: He should be paraded in royal apparel
questions.explanation: The king commanded Haman to take the apparel and horse and parade Mordecai through the city, honoring him. (Esther 6:10)

questions.question: How did Haman view the honor that the king intended for the man he delighted to honor?
options: He thought it was for Mordecai
He thought it was for himself
He thought it was for Esther
questions.correctAnswer: He thought it was for himself
questions.explanation: Haman thought in his heart that the honor was meant for himself when the king asked what should be done for the man he delighted to honor. (Esther 6:6)

questions.question: True or False: Mordecai was honored for saving the king's life.
questions.explanation: Mordecai was honored for having made known the plot of Bigthana and Teresh to kill King Ahasuerus. (Esther 6:2)

questions.question: What literary device is prominently featured in the events of Esther 6 regarding Haman's perspective?
questions.explanation: The chapter is rich in irony as Haman, who planned to hang Mordecai, ends up honoring him instead. (Esther 6:10)

questions.question: Who was seeking to kill King Ahasuerus?
questions.explanation: Bigthana and Teresh were the two chamberlains who sought to lay hands on King Ahasuerus. (Esther 6:2)

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word for 'honor' signify in the context of Esther 6?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'honor' in this context signifies valuing someone highly, as shown by the king's desire to honor Mordecai. (Esther 6:3)

questions.question: What was Haman's initial intention when he came into the king's court?
questions.explanation: Haman entered the court intending to speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on the gallows he had prepared. (Esther 6:4)

questions.question: True or False: Mordecai returned to the king's gate after being honored.
questions.explanation: After being honored, Mordecai returned to the king's gate, indicating he resumed his position after the public honor. (Esther 6:12)

questions.question: Which Old Testament figure does Mordecai's rise to honor parallel in terms of divine favor and reversal of fortunes?
questions.explanation: Mordecai's rise to honor parallels Joseph's story, where both faced persecution but were ultimately exalted by a king due to their faithfulness. (Esther 6:10, Genesis 41:46)

questions.question: What did the king's servants report regarding Mordecai's previous deeds?
questions.explanation: The king's servants reported that Mordecai had saved the king's life by revealing a plot against him. (Esther 6:2)

theological.title: Esther Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Esther Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What prompted King Ahasuerus to command the book of records to be brought to him?
options: He wanted to make a law
questions.explanation: King Ahasuerus could not sleep, leading him to command the book of records to be brought to him (Esther 6:1). This event sets in motion the recognition of Mordecai's loyalty.

questions.question: What had Mordecai previously done that was recorded in the book of chronicles?
options: Saved the king from a conspiracy
questions.correctAnswer: Saved the king from a conspiracy
questions.explanation: Mordecai had reported a conspiracy involving Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king's chamberlains, who sought to harm King Ahasuerus (Esther 6:2).

questions.question: How did King Ahasuerus react upon finding out that nothing had been done for Mordecai?
questions.explanation: Upon learning that nothing had been done for Mordecai, the king expressed a desire to honor him (Esther 6:3).

questions.question: What was Haman doing in the court when summoned by the king?
questions.explanation: Haman had come to the outward court to speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on the gallows he had prepared (Esther 6:4).

questions.question: What did Haman suggest should be done to the man whom the king delights to honor?
options: Let him ride the king's horse
questions.correctAnswer: Let him ride the king's horse
questions.explanation: Haman suggested that the honor should include royal apparel, the king's horse, and a proclamation in the streets (Esther 6:8-9).

questions.question: What was the king's directive to Haman regarding Mordecai?
questions.explanation: The king commanded Haman to take the apparel and horse as he had suggested and to do so for Mordecai (Esther 6:10).

questions.question: What was Haman's reaction after honoring Mordecai?
questions.explanation: After honoring Mordecai, Haman hurried home mourning and with his head covered (Esther 6:12).

questions.question: What did Haman's wise men and Zeresh say about Mordecai's lineage?
questions.explanation: They warned Haman that since Mordecai was of the seed of the Jews, he would not prevail against him (Esther 6:13).

questions.question: How does Esther 6 illustrate God's providential care?
questions.explanation: The king's sleeplessness led to the discovery of Mordecai's loyalty, showing God's providence at work in seemingly ordinary events (Esther 6:1).

questions.question: What does Haman's plan to honor himself reveal about his character?
questions.explanation: Haman believed the king would want to honor him, revealing his pride and arrogance (Esther 6:6-7).

questions.question: What does the king's choice to honor Mordecai teach about justice?
questions.explanation: The king's decision to honor Mordecai demonstrates that justice is fulfilled, even if it takes time (Esther 6:10).

questions.question: How does the narrative reflect the theme of reversal in Esther 6?
options: Mordecai is honored instead of Haman
questions.correctAnswer: Mordecai is honored instead of Haman
questions.explanation: The chapter exemplifies the theme of reversal, where Haman's intention to honor himself turns into Mordecai's honor (Esther 6:10-11).

questions.question: What does Haman's eventual humiliation suggest about pride?
questions.explanation: Haman's pride leads to his eventual humiliation, as he is forced to honor the very man he sought to kill (Esther 6:11-12).

questions.question: In what way does Esther 6 contribute to the understanding of divine sovereignty?
questions.explanation: The events in Esther 6 indicate that despite human intentions, God's sovereign will prevails, as seen in Mordecai's honor (Esther 6:10).

questions.question: What is the significance of the king's chamberlains in the narrative?
questions.explanation: The king's chamberlains play a crucial role in executing the king's orders, which ultimately align with God's providential plan (Esther 6:14).
